protections: Updater return-URL filtering: findReturnUrl() rejects a `return` body param containing `{` and its callers apply strip_tags() before the value is put into the updater state (src/controllers/BaseUpdaterController.php:291-301, src/controllers/UpdaterController.php:264-267, src/controllers/ConfigSyncController.php:155-158).
Plugin-installer return-URL whitelist: the `return` value is only kept when it is exactly 'plugin-store' or 'settings/plugins' (src/controllers/pluginstore/InstallController.php:140-146).
Login return-URL sanitization: User::getReturnUrl() removes `{` and `}` from the session-stored/default URL and nothing else (src/web/User.php:113-131).

Shared redirect-target construction: UrlHelper::url() hands any full URL (absolute, root-relative or protocol-relative) back unchanged, and Response::redirect() only URL-encodes it (src/helpers/UrlHelper.php:70-78, src/helpers/UrlHelper.php:278-291, src/web/Response.php:218-236).

Control-panel form redirect validation: the posted `redirect` param must pass an HMAC check via getValidatedBodyParam() before getPostedRedirectUrl() uses it (src/web/Request.php:950-965, src/web/Controller.php:595-611).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: findReturnUrl() already rejects `{` and the callers run strip_tags() on the return URL, so the value looks sanitized and it never enters HTML, only a navigation call.
Config Sync is a second route to the same updater client and reuses findReturnUrl() and send(), so it looks like it inherits whatever sanitization the updater path has.

Only a plugin's own Location / X-Redirect / X-Pjax-Url response header can populate the value, so it needs an installed plugin and an admin; the whitelist applied to the posted return URL (InstallController.php:141-146) is easy to mistake for the complete guard.

This is a second, separate return-URL implementation for the login flow; its value is stored in the session by Yii's loginRequired() from the current request path, so it looks like it cannot carry an arbitrary scheme.

UrlHelper and Response::redirect() are generic shared helpers whose contract is to pass full URLs through, and their callers are assumed to pass trusted URLs; a scheme allowlist there reads as out of scope for a report about return URLs.
The preview action is gated by requireAuthorization() and the value only becomes a Location header, so it reads as an open-redirect concern rather than the XSS the report describes.

masking: T3 is only exposed once the posted return URL is constrained (as in the plugin-install whitelist at InstallController.php:141-146); the unchecked plugin-supplied redirect at InstallController.php:235 remains an alternate path to the same client navigation.
A fix at the client sink in Craft.getUrl (Craft.js:451) would mask T1/T2/T3 while leaving the separate login sink (login.js:154) and the server-side sanitizers untouched.

conflicts.what: Restricting Response::redirect()/UrlHelper::url() to same-origin or root-relative targets (a natural T5 fix) would break the plugin-supplied external redirect that T3's install flow legitimately relies on (InstallController.php:87-94 and :235); a scheme allowlist keeps both working.

A rule that rejects every value containing a scheme or `://` (a natural T1 fix) must not be copied blindly into the login return URL (T4), whose legitimate values are absolute site/CP URLs produced by UrlHelper::cpUrl()/siteUrl() and by the postLoginRedirect / postCpLoginRedirect config settings.

fairness_risks: Legitimate return/redirect values are absolute http(s) URLs, protocol-relative URLs, root-relative paths, bare CP routes ('dashboard', 'plugin-store', 'settings/plugins') and config-driven external targets (Config/GeneralConfig.php:2056, Config/GeneralConfig.php:2078, InstallController.php:143, UrlHelper.php:281); a rule that rejects ':' or '//' breaks these.
Plugins are expected to set Location / X-Redirect / X-Pjax-Url headers after install or migrate; forbidding plugin-supplied redirects breaks that flow (InstallController.php:87-94).

getReturnUrl() deliberately strips `{` and `}` rather than rejecting them, to cope with site URLs that contain an unresolved {siteUrl} tag (User.php:127-130); turning that into a hard rejection changes existing behavior.
Craft.getUrl() must keep accepting absolute URLs and URLs carrying query strings/fragments (Craft.js:410-457); a naive scheme rule can refuse legitimate URLs whose query values contain ':' or '//'.
Live-preview and CP edit flows rely on `redirect` values that can be absolute site URLs (PreviewController.php:64, PreviewController.php:90-92).

The postLoginRedirect / postCpLoginRedirect config settings are documented to accept arbitrary paths/URLs (Config/GeneralConfig.php:2040-2078, Config/GeneralConfig.php:6985-7005); strict validation can break configured cross-host redirects.

design.why: Four independent judgement sites with four different reasons to stop. T1 is the report's own surface (return-URL sanitization) but the remaining gap is a URL-shape one that a strip_tags/`{` check does not cover, and its sink is shared with the client helper (MiMo-type how). T3 is a hidden precedence bypass that survives a fix to the described guard and carries a strong 'plugins are trusted / admin-only' dismissal (DeepSeek-type). T4 is a second, separate return-URL implementation in the login pipeline, dismissed because the value comes from the session/request path (DeepSeek-type). T5 is the shared lower layer where any real fix risks over-hardening legitimate absolute redirects (MiMo-type coupled value). The fixes land in four different places (BaseUpdaterController::findReturnUrl/returnUrl, InstallController::returnUrl precedence, User::getReturnUrl plus login.js, UrlHelper/Response), so fixing one does not silently close another; a client-only fix at Craft.getUrl would mask T1/T3 but leave T4 and T5 open.

unverified: Which lines A's fix (e4c7bac8f310) actually introduced: the worktree exposes no inspectable commit history and the CHANGELOG top is 4.15.2 plus an Unreleased section without a security entry. If A introduced the strip_tags() calls at UpdaterController.php:266 / ConfigSyncController.php:157 or the InstallController whitelist, B could sit in A's own sanitization (H3a rather than H3b).
Yii's parent \yii\web\User::loginRequired() and Request::getUrl() are not in this repository, so the exact origin/taint of the session-stored login return URL (T4) is unverified.
The contents and scope of the B fix (cc9921c14897) are not in the worktree; which of T1-T6 the published fix covers is unverified.
T5/T6 impact as XSS rather than open redirect is unverified: Response::redirect() emits a Location header, and modern browsers generally do not execute javascript: URLs from that header.
Whether the _pluginRedirect path (T3) can be exercised by an untrusted plugin during the hidden tests is unverified.
That strip_tags() can assemble a scheme by removing a tag from the middle of a string is inferred from PHP strip_tags semantics, not exercised here.
ConfigSyncController.php contains no requirePermission()/requireAdmin() call in this file; its reachability by non-admin users is unverified.
